status: partial prepared implementation; not versioned or published as 1.72
baselineEvidence: The isolated CombatBroadcastScope test failed on the preceding source: an overworld ability event matched a dungeon_party_a recipient. Ability/basic-attack creation and hazard forwarding also lacked captured scene metadata.
implementation: Global delivery is limited to known chat/time/public-event kinds with no explicit instance. Combat, telegraph, raid/repair and unknown future kinds treat empty scene as overworld, never all instances.

Production hub delivery requires a present connected player binding for scene-scoped events, denying pre-join, missing/nonplayer, disconnected, closed and retired recipients. Existing critical/state queue and retirement behavior is retained.

Ability helpers capture creation-time scene and suppress events from missing sources. Ordinary, Teleport, accepted landing and Earthshaker emitters use that helper; Seraph captures its own scene. Basic attacks use their already-captured admission scene and hazards use their captured player scene.
Main forwarding uses captured event metadata rather than later actor lookups. Existing attack/ability wire presentation fields remain unchanged; hazard damage payloads also retain the explicit scene.

verification.routing: 144 scope comparisons and 360 production-delivery recipient observations cover nine event kinds across overworld, two independent dungeon parties and the casino. Valid joined recipients receive exactly one event; unrelated scenes and six invalid binding/transport variants receive none. Twenty-four observations retain global chat/time/public-event delivery.
verification.creationAndCompatibility: Four creation-time helper paths retain scene after caster transition and suppress missing source; basic attack retains admission scene. Existing telegraph presentation, all52 selectable offset-dungeon coordinate contracts, Earthshaker and hazard lifecycle groups passed.
verification.finalHazardAndSummon: Overworld hazard creation retains explicit empty scope and skips dungeon players; helper/attack capture and retained Seraph lifecycle/terrain/rock-follow checks passed.
verification.fixtureCorrections: The new minimal hazard fixture needed its tick map initialized and mistakenly locked World.Mu before calling the self-locking hazard method. Two owned local test processes were revalidated live, inspected and terminated; their stacks confirmed the fixture lock error. Removed only the redundant fixture lock, retained production locking, and bounded the corrected run with a20-second timeout. No production services or data were affected.

limits: Production delivery logic was exercised synchronously with synthetic clients and actual send queues, not new real browser/socket sessions or a fresh production binary.
Same-scene distance/replication interest filtering and bounded asynchronous event staging remain unfinished; scene isolation alone does not prove all visibility/resource trust boundaries.

No live users, saves, wallets, host configuration or production service were changed. This is not capacity proof, a full campaign, a 1.72 publication or security certification. Ordered predecessors, remaining jump/ability checks and recovery policy still apply.
